headline: Analytical choices shape accuracy in MS-based strain, variant and quantity inference
label: Computational Proteomics Benchmarking Methods
summary: Proteomics workflows now embed variant handling, de novo strain calling and quantification choices, each evaluated for its effect on accuracy.
synthesis: The dominant thread is evaluation of how analytical decisions in computational proteomics workflows affect accuracy, from raw mass spectrometry data to protein identifications, strain assignments, or quantities. The DIA-NN workflow for Legionella pneumophila integrates allelic protein sequence variability through clustering and protein inference, targeting single amino acid variants and accessory proteome variability in data-independent acquisition. NovoTax combines de novo peptide sequencing with proteome database search to identify prokaryotic strains directly from raw bottom-up proteomics data. In metaproteomics, MS1 area-under-the-curve quantification is benchmarked against spectral counting, and AUC without match-between-runs is reported to give better accuracy and dynamic range. The items address distinct problems (variant-aware database construction, strain-level identification, and quantification strategy), so the shared element is methodological comparison rather than a single new algorithm class. Novelty lies in the specific design choices examined.
